purpose: Known failures present in the pilot baseline, so that a pilot result can be told apart as KNOWN or NEW (§73). Nothing is hidden to improve a measure. The adjudicator writes the id in the 'known_defect' column when an error matches one of these.
severity_scale: CRITICAL · HIGH · MEDIUM · LOW, the pilot's impact scale (§60); for ordering work, never a score

defects.class: An English order that puts the route before the drug and has no verb
defects.example: IV morphine 4 mg · Nebulized albuterol 2.5 mg · Oral paracetamol 1 g · IV fluids 1 L
defects.what_happens: Read as an order not recognized; the clarification holds the other orders of the submission until it is rephrased. With a verb ('Give nebulized albuterol') it is read.
defects.known_cause: A verbless order must start with the drug or the fluid; a leading route word is not skipped.
defects.why_not_fixed: Not related to DF-16a/b (criterion 1 of §71); found by the held-out check of cycle 4.
defects.pilot_relevance: Low in the Spanish phase (Spanish writes the route after the drug); likely frequent in the English phase.
defects.next_step: Cheap fix before the English documents are collected (cycle 5 proposal).

defects.class: A drug named without a verb and without a dose
defects.example: Morfina ev · Salbutamol nbz · 'Morfina ev y paracetamol 1 g' (the morphine is dropped)
defects.what_happens: Not an order, by the deliberate rule 'a bare drug name is only an order with a command or a dose'; inside a list it is dropped without a word; followed by a repeat, the whole sentence is kept as a repeat instruction.
defects.known_cause: Deliberate conservative rule in family_parser: a verbless drug mention may be narrative ('recibió morfina ev').
defects.why_not_fixed: A design decision (ask for the dose, or ignore) and not a DF-16 defect.
defects.pilot_relevance: Possible in chart shorthand; the pilot will show how often.
defects.next_step: Measure its frequency; then a faculty decision on whether a bare drug with a route should ask for its dose.

defects.class: Text written while a clarification is pending is taken as its answer
defects.example: A route clarification pending for salbutamol, then 'Hidrocortisona 200 mg ev': salbutamol gets 'IV' and the hydrocortisone is not ordered
defects.what_happens: The new order is not executed and its route goes to the held order.
defects.known_cause: The page reads the next submission as the answer to the pending question.
defects.pilot_relevance: None in phase 1: the harness cancels a held order before the next entry (resolve_until_clear).

defects.example: Reevaluar en 15 minutos si puede hablar frases completas
defects.what_happens: The reassessment is kept as a conditional plan and does not run.
defects.known_cause: Every 'si' opens a condition; an indirect question after a reassessment verb is not told apart.
defects.why_not_fixed: Independent of DF-16a/b (DF-16e); to be documented first (faculty, 2026-09-28).
defects.pilot_relevance: Possibly frequent in Spanish reassessment wording ('reevalúo si mejora…'); it would lower reassessment capture.
defects.next_step: Tag it in adjudication; if frequent, a small class fix (cycle 5 proposal).

defects.class: 'OK to discharge' is not read as a discharge
defects.example: OK to discharge with cardiology follow-up
defects.known_cause: The discharge verbs do not include the 'OK to' form.
defects.next_step: Class fix with the English discharge forms.

defects.class: A home prescription joined to the discharge with 'con'/'with' is lost
defects.example: Alta con paracetamol 1 g cada 8 horas · Discharge home with ibuprofen 400 mg every 8 hours
defects.what_happens: The discharge runs; the prescription is not recorded. As a separate list item it is recorded.
defects.known_cause: Only what reads as advice is kept from a discharge's 'with' clause (DF-10).
defects.pilot_relevance: Likely in C05 (renal colic with discharge).
defects.next_step: Keep a prescription from the discharge clause as a prescription.

defects.class: 'Hora' as an appointment is not read as follow-up
defects.example: Alta con hora en policlínico de urología
defects.what_happens: The discharge runs; the follow-up is not recorded.
defects.known_cause: 'hora' is not in the follow-up vocabulary.
defects.next_step: Vocabulary addition when a class fix touches follow-up.

defects.class: Four lines of the held-order message have no Spanish
defects.example: I recognised… · Still to state… · In your own words… · What you already wrote is kept.
defects.what_happens: Shown in English on the Spanish page.
defects.pilot_relevance: None: the pilot does not show the page to physicians.

defects.class: An 'as needed' repeat keeps no condition
defects.example: Give morphine 2 mg IV, repeat every 10 minutes as needed up to 3 doses
defects.what_happens: The repeat keeps its interval and count; 'as needed' / 'según necesidad' is not stored as its condition ('SOS' and 'PRN' are). The text is kept word for word.
defects.known_cause: The repeat's condition words do not include 'as needed'.
defects.why_not_fixed: Whether an 'as needed' is a condition is an annotation question (VC-3 logic); low value before data.
defects.next_step: Decide with the annotation guide; align the reader.

defects.class: A delayed repeat of a study written alone runs now
defects.what_happens: The troponin is requested now. 'Troponina ahora y repetir en 3 horas' runs the troponin and records the repeat.
defects.known_cause: A standalone repeat with only a delay keeps the earlier 'given again now' reading, deliberately, to limit DF-16b's scope.
defects.why_not_fixed: Behaviour unchanged by DF-16b; changing it needs its own review.
defects.next_step: Review with the timed reassessment design.

defects.class: A monitoring instruction is quoted as the working model
defects.what_happens: The Management Trace records the instruction as what the resident thinks is going on.
defects.known_cause: The working-model fallback takes a clause that is not recognised as an order.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found in cycle 4 probes; same family as DF-7, not DF-16.
defects.pilot_relevance: Possible; it would show as an unfaithful slot.
defects.next_step: Class fix in the DF-7 family.

defects.class: A finding outside the closed vocabulary is not read as the working model
defects.example: Hyperkalemia with peaked T waves · Hiperkalemia con T picudas · Still wheezing, …
defects.what_happens: No working model is recorded; the gate asks for it.
defects.known_cause: The findings and appraisal vocabulary is a closed list.
defects.next_step: Let the pilot say which findings matter.

defects.class: Causal and clause-boundary residues in the reasoning
defects.example: 'since' (EN) and 'por' (ES) are not read as a reason · 'to reduce the congestion and I will recheck' keeps 'and I will' in the expectation
defects.what_happens: A reason is missed, or an expectation carries extra words.
defects.known_cause: Both words are ambiguous (temporal 'since', non-causal 'por'); the effect pattern does not stop at 'and I will'.

defects.what_happens: The quote changes spelling, not meaning.
defects.known_cause: Normalization before quoting; pinned by regressions v0814 and v0816.
defects.why_not_fixed: DF-11; the regressions fix the current behaviour.
defects.pilot_relevance: Would show as a not word-for-word quote.
defects.next_step: Decide whether quotes keep the original spelling.

known_behaviour_by_design.class: Oxygen without an absolute flow is held for a clarification, by design
known_behaviour_by_design.example: O2 por mascarilla para saturar sobre 94 %
known_behaviour_by_design.note: Not a defect: the pilot measures whether clinicians find the question unnecessary (DF-16, 'qué no es un defecto').

fixed_in_cycle_4: DF-16c (plural route and a route shared by a list of doses)
